stemMd: Which change generally increases the solubility of a gas in a liquid at fixed temperature, when the gas does not react with the solvent?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Increasing the gas pressure above the liquid

options.label: B
options.textMd: Changing only the colour of the container

options.label: C
options.textMd: Reducing the gas pressure to nearly zero

options.label: D
options.textMd: Removing all gas from above the liquid

options.label: E
options.textMd: Reducing the number of gas molecules available while keeping no reservoir

explanationMd: For many dilute gas solutions, Henry’s law relates dissolved gas concentration to its partial pressure above the liquid. Increasing that pressure favours more gas dissolved at equilibrium. The fixed-temperature and nonreacting-gas conditions are important limitations.

distractorRationale.c: Lower gas pressure generally reduces equilibrium gas solubility.
distractorRationale.d: This tends to drive dissolved gas out.
distractorRationale.b: Colour alone is not the relevant equilibrium variable under fixed temperature.
distractorRationale.e: That does not increase the equilibrium driving force for dissolution.
